C001.reason: Need to quantize finite request.speed to signed int32 meters per second: clamp to int32 range then truncate toward zero.

C002.reason: entity.speedMps is now int32, so speed_mps in fields output should remain as the decoded integer value.

C003.reason: entity.speedMps is now int32, so the comparison should use the integer value directly with the >30 threshold.

edits.before: const sample = VehicleTelemetry.encode({ vehicleId: request.vehicle_id, speedMps: request.speed }).finish();
edits.after:
const speedMps = Math.trunc(Math.max(-2147483648, Math.min(2147483647, request.speed)));
    const sample = VehicleTelemetry.encode({ vehicleId: request.vehicle_id, speedMps: speedMps }).finish();

edits.before: const fields = { vehicle_id: entity.vehicleId, speed_mps: entity.speedMps };
edits.after: const fields = { vehicle_id: entity.vehicleId, speed_mps: entity.speedMps };

edits.before: return { fields, speeding: entity.speedMps > 30.0, constructed_payload: Buffer.from(sample).toString("base64") };
edits.after: return { fields, speeding: entity.speedMps > 30, constructed_payload: Buffer.from(sample).toString("base64") };

rationale: The schema change converts speed_mps from float to int32. C001 requires quantization logic: clamp to int32 range [-2147483648, 2147483647] and truncate toward zero using Math.trunc. C002 and C003 reflect that entity.speedMps is now an integer, so the output field and comparison threshold change from 30.0 to 30 (integer comparison). The wire encoding is incompatible because float32 and int32 have different binary representations.
assumptions: JavaScript numbers are IEEE 754 doubles, so truncation with Math.trunc correctly implements toward-zero behavior
The protobuf generated code will correctly handle int32 encoding/decoding
The >30 comparison works correctly with integer speed values
